_note: Narrative-paraphrase retrieval set. This is NOT the auto-fire gate (see
eval_corpus.json) — nothing here may ever auto-fire, because a paraphrase is
always capped at Suggest. What this measures is RETRIEVAL: when a preacher
TELLS a story instead of quoting it, does Relay surface a verse from the
kjv   — the retelling reuses words that are actually in the KJV text, but
SPREAD ACROSS several verses. No single verse holds them all. This
is the case story-level (windowed) retrieval is supposed to fix.
modern— the retelling uses today's words for KJV concepts ('paralysed' for
'sick of the palsy'). Lexical search cannot fix this at any window
size; only a real sentence embedder will. Tracked so the limit is

cases._comment: The modern block below was authored BEFORE any KJV-modernisation glossary existed, deliberately, so it stays a held-out test rather than a list of things a glossary was fitted to. Natural preacher speech: today's words for 1611 concepts.

cases._comment: scattered: KJV words, but deliberately pulled from verses that do NOT sit together. No single verse holds more than one or two of these fragments, so a per-verse cosine sees only a thin signal while the STORY holds all of them. This is the precise condition story-level retrieval is meant to win, and the only fair test of it.
